old: Rewrote a path before using it: a backslash became a slash, one leading "./" or "/" was dropped, and trailing slashes were dropped, so "a\\b", "./a" and "a/" were taken as "a/b", "a" and "a". A ".." or empty segment was kept as a literal name, and list("") listed every file.
new: Refuses a path that is absolute, contains a backslash or NUL, or has a ".", ".." or empty segment, with a RangeError and before the store is touched. That includes "a\\b", "./a", "a/", ".." and ""; list() with no folder lists every file.
why: One path names one file in every store. The file system store must refuse paths that could leave the workspace, and the memory store follows the same contract so a test can't pass on memory and fail on disk. See also contracts.definition-store and adapter-memory.definition-store.

old: put stored any string as the media type, including parameters ("text/plain; charset=utf-8") and line breaks.
new: put refuses a media type that isn't type/subtype of HTTP token characters, with a RangeError, and stores nothing. A malformed hash (upper case, wrong length, "../etc/passwd") gives null from get, as the old store already did for any unknown hash.
why: A media type ends up in HTTP headers and file metadata; a line break there could split a header. Parameters are left out so one blob has one plain type.

old: append(event) took one event and added it to its run, whatever its seq and whatever was stored before, so two writers could both append and a run could get gaps or repeated numbers.
new: append(runId, expectedSeq, events) adds the events only when the run's last stored seq is expectedSeq, and otherwise returns { ok: false, reason: "conflict", lastSeq } and stores nothing. Empty, misnumbered or other-run events are refused with a RangeError.
why: The run log is the source of truth for a run. Checking expectedSeq means two writers can never interleave events, and of two at the same seq exactly one wins.

old: Checked a value with plain Zod 4.6.7, which has no nesting limit: input nested deeper than the call stack allows threw a RangeError ("Maximum call stack size exceeded") instead of giving issues, and a value that contains itself was accepted.
new: parse first walks the input without recursion and, if it is nested more than 256 keys and indexes deep (MAX_DEPTH) or contains itself, returns one too_deep issue at the path of the first value past the limit, without running the schema. Up to 256 levels it gives the same verdict as plain Zod.
why: A file must never crash the check, and a value that contains itself is never a valid workspace file. Real workspace files are nowhere near 256 levels deep (the old guard schema nested 200 levels still passes), so no file that loaded before is refused now. It is the only schema-kit difference that remains on real Zod; see also schema-kit.old-schema-parity.
